links.outcome: Protocol accuracy of sLLM versus board-certified radiologists against consensus reference standard
links.effect: Overall protocol accuracy 93.1% (566/608) for sLLM vs 91.4% for Rad 3 (P=.23) and 92.1% for Rad 4 (P=.40); contrast accuracy 94.4% vs 92.1% for Rad 3 (P=.027).
links.quote: Overall protocol accuracy was 93.1% (566/608; 95% CI 89.6-96.6) for the sLLM, 91.4% (556/608; 95% CI 87.6-95.3) for Rad 3, and 92.1% (560/608; 95% CI 88.4-95.8) for Rad 4 (sLLM vs Rad 3 P=.23 vs Rad 4 P=.40).

links.outcome: Manual review of discordant sLLM outputs for hallucinations against real patient EMR inputs
links.effect: No clinically significant hallucinations were identified in a manual review of discordant cases.
links.quote: No clinically significant hallucinations were identified in a manual review of discordant cases.

unlisted_practices: LLM augmentation of imaging examination requests with EMR data to improve request completeness (RI-RADS)
Privately hosted institutional secure LLM for protocoling

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of an institutional LLM (Claude 3.5) combined with rule-based parsing to augment MRI exam requests with EMR data and recommend protocols compared to radiologists.
